title: A Ghost for the Deadline
premise: Petra Halloran, a private security contractor who built her career on being untraceable, receives a call on a burner phone she never bought — from her former handler, Daniel Voss, who died eighteen months ago. The voice offers her one job: extract a Russian defector, Irina Sokolova, before a rival syndicate silences her. As Petra follows the trail through Riga and into the mountains of Georgia, she realizes the defector is bait in an elaborate trap designed to flush out Petra herself — because 'Petra Halloran' was never her real identity, but a cover so deep even she has lost track of what lies beneath. In the end, Petra chooses to burn every alias she has ever worn, trading her invisibility for the truth: she delivers Irina to safety, exposes the syndicate's mole inside her own agency, and walks away with nothing but her real name — which she finally speaks aloud.
about_author: Petra Eriksen is the pen name of a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for firms she is still contractually forbidden to name. She lives in Oslo, where she writes thrillers about people who know exactly how surveillance works — and how to fail at it.

chapters.title: The Phone That Wasn't Hers
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. In her Lisbon safehouse, Petra finds a burner phone taped under her sink — a hiding spot she never used. It rings; the voice is Daniel Voss, dead for eighteen months. He says four words: 'They're coming for you.' The emotional beat is cold dread cracking open a carefully sealed life.

chapters.title: Rules of Invisibility
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Flashback-tinged chapter establishing Petra's tradecraft: three years of rotating identities, cash-only living, and a security firm that contracts her precisely because she leaves no trace. Her current client, a paranoid shipping magnate, hints that someone has been asking about 'the woman who doesn't exist.' Beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: A Dead Man's Voice
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. The phone rings again. Voss gives coordinates outside Riga and a deadline: seventy-two hours to extract defector Irina Sokolova. Petra verifies his death certificate, his grave, his dental records — all genuine. Beat: grief weaponized; she decides to go, telling herself it's professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Riga Rain
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Arriving in Riga under a new passport, Petra surveils the extraction point and spots two separate teams watching it — meaning three players, not two. She makes contact with a local fixer, Marta, who warns her that the last contractor who took this job never checked out of his hotel. Beat: hunter realizing she may be prey.

chapters.title: Irina
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Petra meets Sokolova in a church crypt — sharp, terrified, and oddly unsurprised to see her. Irina studies Petra's face too long and says, 'You don't know what you are yet, do you?' Beat: first crack in Petra's certainty about herself; the mission feels staged.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Docks
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. The planned extraction route is a kill box. Petra improvises, saving Irina but losing her gear bag — including the burner phone. Among the attackers' bodies she finds an agency-issue sidearm, traceable to her own firm. Beat: adrenaline curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: The Firm Answers
chapters.summary: POV: Petra / intercut with agency director Callum Reeve. Reeve, in London, learns Petra has gone off-book and orders her flagged as rogue — while quietly assuring an unknown caller that 'the asset is moving as scheduled.' Beat: dramatic irony; the reader sees Petra is a chess piece.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Off-grid in a safehouse, Petra reconstructs her own history and hits gaps: no school records before age nineteen, a first passport issued by a country she can't remember living in. Her memories feel curated. Beat: vertigo — the thriller's identity theme turns inward.

chapters.title: Marta's Price
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Marta agrees to move them south to Georgia — for a price: the truth about who hired her. En route, Irina reveals she was Voss's analyst, and that Voss suspected a mole inside Petra's own agency feeding targets to the syndicate. Beat: reluctant alliance forming under pressure.

chapters.title: Border Crossing
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. A tense night crossing from Turkey into Georgia, bribing a checkpoint officer who recognizes something in Petra's face — 'You served with the Northern Group, didn't you?' Petra has no idea what he means. Beat: her past surfacing in strangers' mouths.

chapters.title: What Voss Buried
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. In Tbilisi, following Voss's coordinates, they find a storage unit: files on a black program called LANTERN that manufactured deep-cover identities — including complete false pasts implanted via memory work. One file folder is labeled HALLORAN, P. Beat: devastating midpoint revelation.

chapters.title: The Woman in the File
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Inside the file: photos of Petra decades younger, under another name, working for the syndicate itself. Either the file is forged to break her, or her entire life since is a constructed legend. Irina urges her to trust the file; Petra wants to burn it. Beat: identity crisis as tactical paralysis.

chapters.title: Reeve's Gambit
chapters.summary: POV: Callum Reeve. Reeve flies to Tbilisi, ostensibly to retrieve Petra, actually to close the operation. We learn he has been selling LANTERN assets' locations to the syndicate for years — and that Voss discovered it, which is why Voss died. Beat: villain fully revealed to reader, not yet to Petra.

chapters.title: Trap Sprung
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. The syndicate hits the safehouse. Marta is killed covering their escape; Irina is taken. Petra escapes wounded, and among the attackers finds the same burner-phone model as hers — dozens of them, pre-programmed. The whole operation was theater staged for her benefit. Beat: rage and humiliation.

chapters.title: Negotiation
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. The phone rings: Reeve himself, offering Irina's life for Petra's surrender and silence about LANTERN. Petra stalls, tracing the call through a compromised cell tower to a mountain fortress in Kazbegi. Beat: cold fury replacing fear; the hunted becomes the planner.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Petra blackmails a disgraced agency colleague, Yusuf, into providing equipment and a window of official blindness. He asks the question that haunts her: 'If the file is true, whose side are you on tonight?' Beat: she stops needing the answer — choice over origin.

chapters.title: The Fortress
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Recon of the Kazbegi compound reveals Reeve meeting the syndicate's broker — and Irina alive, being prepared for interrogation. Petra also learns the final piece: she wasn't just a LANTERN product; she was its prototype, and Voss was the man who stole her out of it. Beat: resolve crystallizing.

chapters.title: Infiltration
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Night assault: Petra enters through the generator line, disables comms, and reaches Irina — who confesses she let herself be captured to get inside and identify the broker's ledger. Beat: trust earned through fire; the bait becomes an ally.

chapters.title: Ledger and Fire
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. They seize the ledger naming every LANTERN asset and every buyer — Reeve's signature throughout. The compound ignites around them as the syndicate burns its own evidence. Petra faces a choice: save the ledger or the wounded Yusuf. She finds a way to do both, barely. Beat: climax begins.

chapters.title: Confrontation on the Ridge
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. On the mountain road, Reeve corners them with a gun and an offer: come back, keep the legend, forget everything. Petra answers by broadcasting the ledger to a journalist's dead-drop and telling him her real name — the one from before LANTERN — aloud, for the first time in twenty years. Reeve hesitates; Yusuf's sniper shot ends him. Beat: climax and catharsis.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Petra delivers Irina and the ledger to the authorities through channels Voss trusted, ensuring the syndicate's network collapses over the following weeks. The agency offers her reinstatement and a new identity. She declines both. Beat: quiet triumph; power refused is power survived.

chapters.title: A Name of Her Own
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Months later, in a small coastal town, Petra lives under no alias at all — unremarkable, findable, free. A stranger asks her name at a café. She gives the real one. Somewhere, a burner phone sits in a drawer, silent. Final beat: identity reclaimed not as a weapon or a shield, but simply as hers.
